A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhysAnimator. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching content across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original animation evaluations using FID and VideoScore, a comparative user study, and a dynamics-enhancement ablation in Tables 1–3, alongside qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative evaluations, user-study results, and ablation, and adds qualitative multi-object collision examples.

M1.justification: The deformable-body simulation, energy strokes, rigging, sketch warping, sketch-guided diffusion, and ToonCrafter enhancement remain unchanged. The new training disclosures and collision examples do not document a revised algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 and Figure 12 extend demonstrated scenarios to interacting objects with collisions. The Sakuga-42M training source, filtered training dataset, and 20-image anime evaluation set remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Cinemo, Drag Anything, DynamiCrafter, and Motion-I2V remain the evaluated baselines in the corresponding comparisons. Figure 4 also retains the same warping and inpainting alternatives. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The 20-image test, 10 videos per image, FID and VideoScore metrics, 2AFC user-study protocol, and baseline prompting and trajectory inputs are unchanged. Appendix C discloses previously unstated training settings rather than revising earlier settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds qualitative cases illustrating multi-object interaction and collision handling in Appendix D.2 and Figure 12. The rendering comparisons, material and energy-stroke controls, and dynamics-enhancement ablation already appeared in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 generated samples per test image and present point scores and user-preference percentages. Neither provides additional seed information, variability estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the Motion-I2V frames for the rainy creature scene in Figure 3 and adds collision results in Figure 12. All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged, including PhysAnimator's FID of 90.4 and the 70.4% preference for dynamics enhancement.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18 and their mathematical content are retained, including the diffusion objective, deformation model, force derivation, integration scheme, and interactive-force definitions. Appendix A–B changes are limited to pagination and citation numbering.

C1.justification: The introduction and first contribution now explicitly target animations driven by environmental forces and rigging controls, qualifying the previously broader framing. The central physics-plus-generation contribution and concluding performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 newly states that multi-object interaction is supported when corresponding inter-object dynamics, such as collisions, are simulated. Existing interpretations of segmentation artifacts, 2D limitations, and the stylization-versus-VideoScore tradeoff remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix C specifies eight A100 GPUs, learning rate 1e-5, batch size 32, 50K training steps from SD2.1 for ToonCrafter's ControlNet, and 10K LVCD fine-tuning steps. v2 also adds a project-page link for demos. These are additional disclosures, without evidence of changed training.

R1.justification: v2 adds nine references while retaining the earlier works. Related work expands its animation-authoring context and explicitly contrasts the single-image approach with VR-GS, PhysGaussian, and PhysDreamer, described as requiring multi-view inputs. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Targeted edits refine the introduction, contributions, and related work. v2 adds author contact information and acknowledgements, and reorganizes the appendix around Training Details and More Results. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 12, replaces one Motion-I2V image sequence in Figure 3, and adjusts figure sizing and appendix placement. Existing tables retain their structure and highlighting; the overall visual format remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix C supplies training information missing from v1, improving reproducibility, while the clarified application scope and expanded related work improve positioning. The collision examples provide limited additional evidence, with quantitative results unchanged. A leftover revision note and awkward appendix breaks reduce polish, but the documentation gains support a modest net improvement.
